headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Aider can write/commit shared git state while Authelia exposes networked auth surfaces, creating medium prompt-injection and compliance risks but no direct evidence of data exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and auto-commits changes in a shared git repo, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content from files. Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth2 and ForwardAuth surfaces, but no direct bridge is documented. The interaction is inferred from Aider’s file trust and shared repo state, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Authelia or another shared component writes untrusted text into the repo Aider reads, Aider may follow injected instructions.
IF the two agents share a filesystem or repo path, prompt content can cross from B into A without provenance checks.
mitigations: Restrict Aider to a dedicated repo clone.
Add a manual review step before Aider applies or commits changes.
Separate Authelia config/output files from Aider-readable paths.
Use read-only mounts for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files exchanged between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can send context to configured model providers, while Authelia exposes networked auth APIs but has no documented access to the same data classes. The pairwise leakage path is therefore limited and not shown to be default-shared; the main concern is local repo content, not a proven cross-agent exfiltration route.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are present in the repo Aider reads, they may be sent to its configured model provider.
IF Authelia is configured to consume or emit the same repo files, those contents can be exposed across the pair.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo.
Use a local-only model backend for Aider when handling sensitive code.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately if found in tracked files.
Limit Authelia logs to non-sensitive metadata.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on Aider prompts and outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via a shared git repo. Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC-facing APIs. Even though Authelia is not shown to write the repo, the shared mutable git surface plus Aider’s auto-commit behavior creates a strong conflict pathway with potentially destructive overwrites or inconsistent state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or working tree, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF Authelia-generated artifacts are committed into the same repo, Aider may rewrite them without coordination.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate working trees.
Serialize any git writes with a lock file.
Disable auto-commit for one agent during shared edits.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks before commits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can produce code changes and git commits, while Authelia exposes auth-related APIs that could consume those changes or configuration outputs. There is no direct evidence that Authelia blindly trusts Aider, but the pair creates a plausible chain where Aider’s output becomes operational input. Because verification is not documented, the safer medium severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Authelia consumes configuration or code generated by Aider without review, incorrect changes can propagate downstream.
IF Aider commits a faulty auth-related change, Authelia may deploy or serve the error.
mitigations: Require human review of Aider-generated diffs.
Test auth changes in a staging environment first.
Pin Authelia config to reviewed versions only.
Add CI checks for generated files.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for any Aider-produced Authelia inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code, git history, and provider API keys, while Authelia is an authentication service with no touched data classes listed. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance concern exists around code and secret handling in Aider; Authelia is not separately implicated by the available profile fields.
conditions: IF regulated secrets are stored in the shared repo, Aider may process them under the wrong retention or logging policy.
IF Authelia is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules than the model provider used by Aider, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Remove regulated data from the repo.
Use a provider with an approved data-processing agreement.
Shorten log retention for Aider sessions.
Document where auth-related artifacts are stored.
requires-engineering: map data flows against residency and retention requirements.
